resources.string: Tap or drag edges to draw one closed loop. Start on a drawn edge to erase. Numbers count surrounding edges.
Fill cells so every row and column matches its ordered number clues. Each clue describes one uninterrupted run, with at least one empty cell between runs.
Tap or drag to fill cells. Begin a drag on a filled cell to erase. Long-press a cell to add or remove an X mark.
Start with lines whose runs and required gaps nearly fill the available length, then use completed lines to constrain their crossings.
Crack the hidden ordered color code within the available guesses. The level details state whether the code may contain duplicate colors.

Tap a slot, then choose a color swatch. Fill every slot and submit the guess. A solid feedback peg means correct color and position; a ring means correct color in another position. Feedback pegs are unordered and do not correspond to individual slots.
Compare the total feedback between guesses and remember that moving a color can change both exact and misplaced counts.
Turn every light off. Pressing one light changes that light and its orthogonal neighbors above, below, left, and right.
Tap any board cell to toggle its cross-shaped group. Reset restores the starting pattern.
Pressing the same cell twice cancels itself. A useful approach is to work row by row, using each row to clear the one above it.
Fill every white cell with digits 1–9. Each horizontal and vertical run must total its clue, and a digit cannot repeat within one run.
Tap a white cell, then choose a digit. Use X to clear it. Split clue cells show the sums for the runs extending right and down.
List the possible digit combinations for a run from its sum and length, then use crossing runs to remove possibilities.
Use every clue to determine the unique one-to-one match between items in each category.
Tap a comparison cell to cycle through check, cross, and blank. A check records a confirmed match; a cross rules a match out.
Whenever one match is confirmed, cross out every other option in the same row and column before applying the next clue.
Draw one closed loop along grid edges. The loop cannot branch or cross, and each number states exactly how many of its surrounding edges belong to the loop.
Tap an edge to draw or erase it. Drag across edges to fill continuously; begin on a drawn edge to erase while dragging.
Resolve 0 and 3 clues early, avoid creating branches, and do not close a smaller loop while unused loop sections remain.
Leave one unshaded island around each number, with exactly that many cells. All shaded cells form one connected river, islands cannot touch orthogonally, and the river cannot contain a 2×2 block.
Tap or drag across unnumbered cells to shade or unshade them. Numbered cells always remain part of their islands.
Shade cells between neighboring numbered islands first, and watch island sizes so they cannot grow beyond their clues.
Fill the board with consecutive numbers from 1 to the final value. Every number must touch the next one horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.
Tap an empty cell, enter its digits, then confirm. Use delete to correct the current entry. Fixed clues cannot be changed.
Work forward and backward from fixed clues. Narrow spaces between nearby clues often force the only possible route.
Fill each row, column, and marked region with every allowed value exactly once. Every inequality between neighboring cells must also be true.
Tap an editable cell and choose a value from the keypad. Use X to clear it. The open side of an inequality faces the larger value, while its point faces the smaller value.
Combine missing-value checks with inequality chains. Values near either end of the range are often forced by long chains.

Place each available building height once in every row and column. Edge clues count visible buildings from that direction because taller buildings hide shorter ones. Levels with empty lots require the stated number of X cells in each row and column.
Tap a cell and select a height or X from the keypad. Buildings and Numbers changes only how placed heights are displayed; it does not change the puzzle or its values.
The tallest building blocks everything behind it. A clue of 1 puts the tallest building first, while the maximum clue requires heights to rise from that side.
